officialInventory.summary: State protected areas are managed by the Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism (MEFT); its website lists 20 state protected areas (national parks, game parks, recreation resorts, Cape Cross Seal Reserve, South West Nature Reserve) with size and proclamation year per park, but no machine-readable register and no Government Notice references. Communal conservancies are registered by MEFT under s.24A of the Nature Conservation Ordinance; the most complete public list is NACSO's table (86 conservancies, matching MEFT's stated 86) plus NACSO's compilation of gazette numbers. A further conservancy (Ekango Lyomongwa) was gazetted in September 2025. Community forests (Forest Act 2001) and inland fisheries reserves (Inland Fisheries Resources Act 2003) were enumerated directly from the Government Gazettes hosted by NACSO. The marine protected area is the Namibian Islands' Marine Protected Area (Marine Resources Act 2000).

statedCounts.quote: Namibia has 20 state run protected areas coverring about 17 per cent of the country's land surface
at present there are 86 registered by the MET, covering 19.6% of the country
There are currently 43 registered and emerging community forests across ten regions in northern Namibia
There are currently 10 gazetted reserves in Namibia, all in the Zambezi region

gaps: MEFT gives proclamation years and sizes but not the Government Notice numbers for the 20 state protected areas; the specific notices (e.g. Bwabwata 2007, Dorob 2010, Tsau //Khaeb 2008, Mangetti 2008, Nkasa Rupara renaming) were not verified (NamibLII was behind a bot challenge).
'South West Nature Reserve' appears in MEFT's list but its link points to the Skeleton Coast page; its location, size and legal basis could not be verified.

MEFT's state-protected-area list does not include the Namibian Islands' Marine Protected Area, Cape Cross is listed as a 'Seal Reserve', and Gross-Barmen / Hardap / Von Bach / Naute are recreation-oriented game parks or resorts; categories here follow MEFT labels.
Conservancy registrations after 2018 other than Ekango Lyomongwa (GN 248 of 2025) could not be checked systematically; the NACSO/MEFT count of 86 may be out of date.

NACSO says '43 registered and emerging' community forests, but 47 gazetted declarations (2006-2023) were found in the gazettes NACSO hosts; the gazette list is used here and community forests declared outside these gazettes may be missing.
GN 297 of 2016 declares the whole Zambezi/Chobe River system a seasonal fisheries reserve (1 December to 28 February each year); it is a seasonal closure and is not recorded as an area.

No official coordinates were used; points depend on Wikidata matches. Wikidata was heavily rate-limited (HTTP 429) during this run, so only a keyword search (haswbstatement:P17) was possible; most conservancies, community forests and fisheries reserves appear to have no Wikidata item and have null QIDs.
